paragraphs.notes: The cells are chemical symbols and abbreviations, not German prose, so zh and en carry the same string; this is the convention the instructions set for enumeration tables. The page body is nothing but this table: no Tabelle caption, no scaffold drawing, no prose, and no footer. The caption that fixes the shared substituents and draws the scaffold is on an earlier page, so what R7a, R7b, R12, L and R1 attach to is not determinable from this page alone. The column heads are printed with superscripts (R with a raised 7a, 7b, 12 and 1); they are flattened to R7a, R7b, R12 and R1 here. Likewise the 2 in SO2, CH2 and PhC(O)CH2 is printed as a subscript and is flattened. Numbering runs 98 to 124 without a gap, 27 rows, and the R7a/R7b pairs cycle H,H then H,Me then Me,Me; row 98 is the Me,Me row completing a triple that began on the previous page, and row 124 is a H,Me row whose Me,Me partner falls on the next page. R1 is O-c-Bu for rows 98 to 101 and O-c-Pr from row 102 on. 'Bz' is printed as such in rows 102 to 104 and 108 to 110 and is transcribed as printed, not expanded: in this document's own usage it is the benzoyl group, but nothing on this page states that, so it is left as the printed token. The R12 text in row 121 is indented about one character further right than the PhSO2 in rows 120 and 122; that is print registration, not a different value. A small ink blot sits against the top right of the 'O' in row 99's O-c-Bu cell; it is a scan artifact, not a character, and the cell reads O-c-Bu like the three rows around it.
